text:
PHI arrives in Detroit having been outplayed in most of its eight games. The Flyers' expected goals share at five-on-five is just 35 percent, and they allow 3.72 expected goals per 60 minutes against 2.15 created. Their last five games produced one goal in four of them, and two of those losses came with an expected goals share under a third. DET is roughly even (3.24 created, 3.25 allowed, a 51 percent share), and the Red Wings have been the better team on the chance ledger in four of their last five, even though two of those ended in losses. The model sees DET scoring 3.15 goals tonight to PHI's 2.74.

Special teams lean toward Detroit. The Red Wings generate 0.91 expected power-play goals a game to the Flyers' 0.54, and they draw 4.5 penalties a game, so PHI's 4.62 minors taken per game gives that edge room to matter. Both penalty kills are leaking about three-quarters of an expected goal a game. Both teams played Tuesday, so rest is equal.

Neither projected starter has found form. Dan Vladar (PHI) sits at an .880 save percentage and minus 2.54 goals saved above expected, and John Gibson (DET) is at .860 and minus 3.14. Last season both were strong, at plus 12.74 over 52 games and plus 10.11 over 57, so the early numbers may just be noise. Among skaters, the model likes Alex DeBrincat most, with a 39 percent chance to score and 27 percent for two or more points. Dylan Larkin and Viktor Arvidsson are each at 34 percent to score. For PHI, Tyson Foerster is at 25 percent and Trevor Zegras at 24 percent.
